chapters.title: Christ supreme and his people reconciled

parts.text: Paul thanks God for the Colossians’ faith, love, and heavenly hope, learned through Epaphras’s gospel ministry. He prays for knowledge of God’s will, fruitful conduct, endurance, and gratitude. The Father has rescued them from darkness into his Son’s kingdom, where Christ’s blood brings redemption and forgiveness. Christ is the invisible God’s image, the creator and sustainer of all things, and head of the church. All fullness dwells in him, and peace and reconciliation come through his cross.

Those once alienated by wicked works have been reconciled through Christ’s bodily death, to be presented holy if they remain grounded in the gospel’s hope. Paul rejoices in suffering for Christ’s body and describes his commission to reveal the formerly hidden mystery: Christ in them, the hope of glory, among the Gentiles. He warns and teaches everyone toward maturity in Christ, laboring through God’s power within him.

Paul labors for believers to be encouraged, united in love, and assured in understanding Christ, in whom all wisdom and knowledge are hidden. They must remain rooted in him and resist persuasive traditions and empty philosophy. All the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily in Christ, and they are complete in him. Paul describes their spiritual circumcision, burial and resurrection with Christ through faith, forgiveness, removal of the condemning ordinances at the cross, and Christ’s triumph over powers.

No one should judge them over food, drink, or sacred days, which are shadows whose substance belongs to Christ. They must resist false humility and angel worship that lose hold of Christ, the head nourishing his body. Having died with Christ to the world’s rudiments, they should not submit to human regulations about handling or tasting perishable things merely because these display an appearance of wisdom and self-denial.

chapters.title: The life above and daily conduct

parts.text: Raised with Christ, believers should set their desires on heavenly things, where he sits at God’s right hand; their hidden life will appear with him in glory. They must put to death sexual sin, evil desires, and covetousness, and discard anger, malice, foul speech, and lying. The renewed person bears the Creator’s image, with Christ central across human divisions. Compassion, humility, patience, forgiveness, love, peace, gratitude, and Christ’s indwelling word should shape their worship and conduct.

Paul applies this life to households: wives should submit fittingly, husbands love without bitterness, children obey, and fathers avoid discouraging them. Servants should work sincerely rather than merely when watched, doing everything heartily for the Lord. Their ultimate reward comes from Christ, whom they serve. Wrongdoing will receive its due without favoritism.

chapters.title: Prayer, wise speech, and fellow workers

parts.text: Paul tells masters to treat servants justly and fairly, remembering their own Master in heaven. He calls for steadfast, watchful prayer with thanksgiving and asks that God open opportunities for him to explain Christ’s mystery clearly despite his imprisonment. Believers should act wisely toward outsiders, making good use of opportunities and speaking graciously so they can answer each person appropriately.

Tychicus and Onesimus will report Paul’s circumstances and encourage the church. Paul sends greetings from fellow workers, commending Epaphras’s earnest prayers for their maturity and zeal for neighboring churches. He also greets Laodicea and the church in Nymphas’s house. The Colossians must exchange letters with Laodicea, and Archippus must fulfill his received ministry. Paul adds his own greeting, asks them to remember his bonds, and closes with grace.
